# Implement block: Velocity Marquee (React Native)

You are adding the "Velocity Marquee" block from Native Cook to the user's React Native app. The block already exists as working code. Your job is to bring it into this project faithfully, not to write a new one that looks similar.

## The block

An onboarding screen for an invented photo app, on warm off-white paper with a fine grain. Under a small mark and the "Afterimage" wordmark, three rows of rounded photo tiles tilted about 8 degrees, rising to the right, run as endless marquees, the middle row the other way. Below them sit page dots, a short semibold headline with a line of body text under it, a full-width black "Get started" pill and an "Already have an account? Sign in" line. Swiping through the three pages throws the rows with the finger's speed: they race, the tiles lean into the motion like italic type and stretch, then ease back to the idle drift while the headline slides across to the next page and the wide page dot moves with it.

**Motion.** The paper and its 128-texel tile of seeded grain (one texel per 0.5 pt) are drawn once on a layer of their own; the rows are drawn on one canvas above it. The rows fill the space between the brand line and the text block, 18 pt clear of each, centred in it; each is turned −8° about its own centre line and they sit 112 pt apart, shrinking together (to no less than 72%) on a screen too short for them. Tiles are 96 pt tall, 72 pt wide for portraits and 134 pt for landscapes, 12 pt apart with 18 pt corners; each row repeats after its twelve tiles, and rows of different lengths travel at speeds in proportion to their length so all of them repeat together. Idle, the rows drift at 40 pt/s, row one leftwards. Dragging moves every row with the finger (horizontal travel plus 40% of vertical), each in its own direction; on release the rows are thrown at the finger's speed (up to 6000 pt/s), which eases back to the drift on a critically damped spring of natural frequency 3.2/s (stiffness 10.24, damping 6.4), v(t) = v0(1 + 3.2t)e^(−3.2t). Touching the rows catches them. The tiles lean on an underdamped spring (stiffness 140, damping 11.8) that chases the speed, 0.0055° of skew per pt/s up to 16°, the tops leading in each row's direction, so they overshoot a little and wobble upright as the rows slow; they also stretch along the row by 0.004% per pt/s up to 12% and thin by a third of that. A release that went mostly sideways turns the page when it travelled 18% of the width or is faster than 450 pt/s (leftwards to the next page, no wrap at either end), with one selection haptic; the page settles on a critically damped spring of 560 ms. Each page's headline and line slide 28 pt with the page and fade out by 0.46 of a page away, so the old text has gone before the new one arrives; the page dot of the page shown widens from 6 to 20 pt and darkens from 20% to full ink as the page arrives. The button squeezes to 0.97 on a spring (stiffness 420, damping 26) with a light haptic on touch down; the sign-in line dims to 45% in 100 ms while pressed. Entrance: once laid out, the rows fade in over 0.9 s while rising 14 pt (ease-out 0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), and the dots, the text, the button and the sign-in line fade in and rise 10 pt over 0.6 s, 220 ms after the rows start and 90 ms apart; each photo fades in over 0.45 s as it loads, and one that fails stays a paper-coloured tile. The self-playing demo loops every 15 s: each page rests, then at 3.2, 8.2 and 13.2 s a swipe to the next page pushes the rows leftwards (a 0.28 s smoothstep to a peak of about 1650 pt/s, then the release spring) and the page turns over 0.6 s (cubic ease-out) from the release; the third swipe carries the last page round to the first. The peak is set so the rows travel exactly three row lengths per loop, and each swipe's speed counts the tail of the same swipe from the loop before, so the rows, their speed and the page meet the first frame on the last. A touch stops it for 3 s, then the loop starts over from where things are. Under reduced motion the rows hold still and follow a drag one to one, with no throw, lean, stretch or rise, the pages cross-fade over 320 ms, and the demo does not play.

## Reference source

The block is built and running in the Native Cook source repository. Each link below is a file on GitHub. To read one as plain text, replace `https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/` with `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/` in its address.

### Demo (start here)

- [index.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/onboarding/velocity-marquee/index.tsx)

### Files of the block

- [VelocityMarquee.tsx](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/onboarding/velocity-marquee/VelocityMarquee.tsx)
- [VelocityMarqueePhotos.ts](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/src/blocks/onboarding/velocity-marquee/VelocityMarqueePhotos.ts)

### Packages

- `expo-haptics`
- `expo-status-bar`

The versions the block was built with are in [react-native/package.json](https://github.com/Native-Cook/native-cook/blob/main/react-native/package.json).

## Your instructions

_Anything specific to this app goes here: where the block should appear, what to rename, what to change. Left empty, integrate the block as it is._

## How to work

Work like an experienced React Native engineer joining an existing project: learn the app first, read only what you need, decide early how the block fits, then integrate it with as little disruption as possible. Take the steps in order.

**Done means** the block is reachable in the user's app and behaves like the reference on iOS or Android: a simulator, an emulator or a device. A browser is never proof. Do not open the app on the web to check it, not even when the mobile build fails.

**Fidelity.** Bring over the real implementation. Keep its structure, colours, sizes, timings and easing. Change only what this project requires and what "Your instructions" ask for.

If you already learned this project earlier in the conversation, reuse what you know and skip step 2. Learn it again only if the project changed or something you need is missing.

### 1. Check where you are

- You need the project's files and a terminal. If this prompt was pasted into a chat that has neither, stop and say so: it has to be run by a coding agent opened on the project.
- Confirm the project is a React Native app, Expo or bare. If it is something else, stop, say what you found, and do not create a new app inside it unless the instructions ask for one.

### 2. Learn the host app

- Expo (managed or prebuild) or bare React Native, and the versions of React Native and the Expo SDK.
- The package manager, and how the app is started: Expo Go, a development build, or `react-native run-ios` / `run-android`.
- Navigation: Expo Router, React Navigation, something else, or a single screen. Find how a screen is added today.
- Conventions: TypeScript or not, path aliases, how styles are written, where components and screens live.
- Which of the block's packages are already installed, and at which versions.

### 3. Read the block

- Open the demo, then each file it imports. The list above names every file of the block, so you do not have to guess.
- The demo is how the source repository shows the block. Bring over what the demo renders, not the repository's gallery. Anything listed under "Used by the demo only" stays behind.
- Read the block's props and their defaults. The demo may switch on an option that makes the block play by itself for a recording (for example `autoPlay`). Keep the option; leave it off in the user's app unless asked.

### 4. Decide the fit

- Compare the block's packages with the host's. Install what is missing with the project's own tool (`npx expo install …` in an Expo app, so versions match its SDK).
- A package with native code needs a new native build, and Expo Go only runs the modules it ships with. Say so before you install one, and say which build the user will need.
- If the host is on older versions and an API differs, adapt the block's code to the host. Do not upgrade the host's React Native, Expo SDK or animation libraries without asking.
- Put the files where this app keeps its components. Ask only when two places are equally reasonable and the choice matters.

### 5. Bring it in

- Copy the block's files, keep their names, and rewrite imports to this project's paths and aliases.
- Copy its images and fonts with it, and load fonts the way the project already does.
- Keep reduced-motion handling, haptics and accessibility labels as they are in the source.
- Mount the block where the instructions say. With no instructions, add a screen or route named after the block and make it reachable the way the app's other screens are.

### 6. Run it

- Typecheck and lint with the project's own commands and fix what the block introduced.
- Run the app on the user's usual mobile target and use the block: every state, every gesture, and once with reduced motion on.
- If the simulator, the emulator or the native build fails, report the error and ask how to continue. Do not fall back to the web.

### 7. Report

- Files added and changed, packages installed, and whether a new native build is needed.
- How to reach the block in the app.
- Anything that differs from the reference, and why.
